== ConLeche/Denotes.lean#L248-L268
   248  structure Model (V : Type w) [SetTheory V] (env : Env) where
   249    /-- the set a constant denotes, per level assignment -/
   250    cval : Name → (LevelParam → Nat) → V
   251    /-- every stored constant is a member of what its type denotes, at
   252    every level assignment (and every variable environment — the type
   253    is closed) -/
   254    mem : ∀ c ∈ env.consts, ∀ (φ : LevelParam → Nat) (ρ : BVarIdx → V),
   255      ∃ T, Denotes cval env φ ρ c.toConstantVal.type T ∧ cval c.name φ ∈ˢ T
   256    /-- whatever the built-in `False` denotes is the empty set -/
   257    false_empty : ∀ (φ : LevelParam → Nat) (ρ : BVarIdx → V) (F : V),
   258      Denotes cval env φ ρ (.const falseName []) F → F = empty
   259    /-- whatever the built-in `Eq` denotes is set equality: at a type `A`
   260    of the universe the level `u` names, and two of its members `a` and
   261    `b`, `@Eq.{u} A a b` denotes the truth value of `a = b`.  The three
   262    membership premises are the graph's domains — `Eq`'s denotation is a
   263    three-fold graph over `univ (Level.eval φ u)`, then over `A`, then
   264    over `A` again, and a graph read off its domain says nothing -/
   265    eq_equality : ∀ (u : Level) (φ : LevelParam → Nat) (ρ : BVarIdx → V) (E A a b : V),
   266      Denotes cval env φ ρ (.const eqName [u]) E →
   267      A ∈ˢ univ (Level.eval φ u) → a ∈ˢ A → b ∈ˢ A →
   268      app (app (app E A) a) b = eqv a b

== ConLeche/Accepts.lean#L62-L72
    62  def jsonWithTheoremFalse (chunks : List ByteArray) : Prop :=
    63    ∃ (before between₁ between₂ between₃ after name : String) (i j k v : Nat),
    64      Frontend.concatBytes chunks = (s!"{before}
    65  \{\"in\":{i},\"str\":\{\"pre\":0,\"str\":\"False\"}}
    66  {between₁}
    67  \{\"ie\":{j},\"const\":\{\"name\":{i},\"us\":[]}}
    68  {between₂}
    69  \{\"in\":{k},\"str\":\{\"pre\":0,\"str\":\"{name}\"}}
    70  {between₃}
    71  \{\"thm\":\{\"all\":[{k}],\"levelParams\":[],\"name\":{k},\"type\":{j},\"value\":{v}}}
    72  {after}").toUTF8

== ConLeche/Model/StreamConsts.lean#L89-L95
    89  @[expose] def Declaration.Declares : Declaration → ConstantVal → Prop
    90    | .defnDecl cv _ _, cv' => cv' = cv
    91    | .thmDecl cv _, cv' => cv' = cv
    92    | .opaqueDecl cv _, cv' => cv' = cv
    93    | .axiomDecl cv, cv' => cv' = cv ∧ cv.name ≠ sorryAxName ∧ cv.name ≠ quotSoundName
    94    | .indDecl _ _, _ => False
    95    | .quotDecl _ _, _ => False

== ConLeche/Kernel/Install.lean#L85-L97
    85  def declConstants : Declaration → List ConstantInfo
    86    | .defnDecl cv value hint => [.defnInfo cv value hint]
    87    | .thmDecl cv _ => [.thmInfo cv]
    88    | .opaqueDecl cv _ => [.axiomInfo cv]
    89    | .axiomDecl cv =>
    90      if cv.name = quotSoundName then [quotAt .sound cv]
    91      else if cv.name = sorryAxName then []
    92      else [.axiomInfo cv]
    93    | .quotDecl k cv => [quotAt k cv]
    94    | .indDecl block nP =>
    95      match readBlock nP block with
    96      | .ok p => blockConstants p
    97      | .error _ => []

    29  def whnfCore (env : Env) (fuel depth : Nat) (e : Expr) (cheap : Bool := false) :
    30      CheckM Expr :=
    31    (pureFns mode eager env fuel).whnfCore cheap depth e
    32  
    33  /-- The full reduction loop (fueled). -/
    34  def whnf (env : Env) (fuel depth : Nat) (e : Expr) : CheckM Expr :=
    35    (pureFns mode eager env fuel).whnf depth e
    36  
    37  /-- Full-grade type inference (fueled): the declaration front door's
    38  entry — official's `infer_type_core(e, infer_only = false)`. -/
    39  def inferTypeCore (env : Env) (fuel depth : Nat) (e : Expr) : CheckM Expr :=
    40    (pureFns mode eager env fuel).infer depth e
    41  
    42  /-- Type inference at the io grade (fueled): the knot's `inferIO` slot
    43  — what every internal inference call site runs (task #170).  At every
    44  mode it is the io lane (`inferTypeIO_on`, `Verify/Knot.lean`). -/
    45  def inferTypeIO (env : Env) (fuel depth : Nat) (e : Expr) : CheckM Expr :=
    46    (pureFns mode eager env fuel).inferIO depth e

    50    (pureFns mode eager env fuel).defeq depth a b
    51  
    52  /-- `ensureSort` over the pure knot (fueled). -/
    53  def ensureSortCore (env : Env) (fuel depth : Nat) (e : Expr) : CheckM Level :=
    54    ensureSort (pureFns mode eager env fuel) env depth e

== ConLeche/Kernel/Core.lean#L2313-L2331
  2313  def defeqBody (eager : Bool) (r : CoreFns m) (env : Env) : Nat → Expr → Expr → m Bool :=
  2314    fun depth a b => do
  2315      if a == b then pure true else
  2316      match ctorTargetFor env eager a b with
  2317      | some c =>
  2318        let w ← r.whnf depth a
  2319        match ctorHeadAgainst env c w with
  2320        | some true => defeqLazy mode eager r env depth w b
  2321        | some false => pure false
  2322        | none => defeqLazy mode eager r env depth a b
  2323      | none =>
  2324      match ctorTargetFor env eager b a with
  2325      | some c =>
  2326        let w ← r.whnf depth b
  2327        match ctorHeadAgainst env c w with
  2328        | some true => defeqLazy mode eager r env depth a w
  2329        | some false => pure false
  2330        | none => defeqLazy mode eager r env depth a b
  2331      | none => defeqLazy mode eager r env depth a b

== ConLeche/Kernel/Core.lean#L2218-L2227
  2218  def rulesLast (r : CoreFns m) (env : Env) (depth : Nat) (oa ob : Option Expr) (a b : Expr) :
  2219      m Bool := do
  2220    let ra ← originFire r env depth oa a
  2221    let rb ← originFire r env depth ob b
  2222    match ra, rb with
  2223    | none, none => pure false
  2224    | some (_, a₂), none => r.defeq depth a₂ b
  2225    | none, some (_, b₂) => r.defeq depth a b₂
  2226    | some (_, a₂), some (_, b₂) => r.defeq depth a₂ b₂
  2227

== ConLeche/Kernel/Exclusive.lean#L6-L42
     6  # `withExclusive`: the reference-count read behind the walk memo
     7  
     8  **What it is.**  `withExclusive a k h` runs the continuation `k` on
     9  whether the object `a` is *exclusive* — single-threaded with reference
    10  count exactly 1, so that no other reference to it exists.  In the logic
    11  it is `k false` ("not known to be exclusive", the conservative answer);
    12  in compiled code `@[implemented_by]` substitutes `k
    13  (isExclusiveUnsafe a)`, the real count read off the object header
    14  (`Init/Util.lean`, `@[extern "lean_is_exclusive_obj"]`, a BORROWED
    15  parameter; `lean_is_exclusive` in `lean.h`).  A multi-threaded object
    16  (count `< 0`) and a persistent one (count `0` — the installed
    17  environment after the driver's `Runtime.markPersistent`) answer
    18  `false`, which is the safe side.
    19  
    20  **What justifies the substitution** is the obligation
    21  
    22  ```
    23  h : k true = k false
    24  ```
    25  
    26  — the continuation's value does not depend on the answer, so the
    27  compiled program computes the very value the definition names.  A
    28  caller may use the answer to choose *how* to compute a value, never
    29  *which* value.  `Init.Util`'s `withPtrAddr` is the same arrangement
    30  (`k 0` in the model, the address in the binary, the continuation
    31  address-blind by obligation), and `Bool` being two-valued makes
    32  `k true = k false` the whole of `∀ b₁ b₂, k b₁ = k b₂`.
    33  
    34  **What it is for.**  The per-walk memo tables of the substitution walks
    35  (`ConLeche/Cached/ExprOpsC.lean`) exist for one reason: a node reached
    36  twice — a shared sub-DAG — must be rebuilt once, so that the walk is
    37  `O(DAG)` and its OUTPUT stays shared.  A node with exactly one
    38  reference cannot be reached twice, so recording it is pure loss: the
    39  key, the entry, the probe.  The official kernel's `replace_fn`
    40  (`src/kernel/replace_fn.cpp`) therefore caches a node's replacement
    41  only when `!is_likely_unshared(e)` — the same read.  The walks memoise
    42  exactly the nodes this primitive reports shared.

== ConLeche/Term/Syntax.lean#L188-L219
   188  inductive Term where
   189    /-- de Bruijn index -/
   190    | bvar (i : Nat)
   191    /-- `Sort u` at a concrete level -/
   192    | sort (u : Nat)
   193    /-- a built-in constant at a concrete level instantiation -/
   194    | const (c : BConst) (us : List Nat)
   195    /-- application -/
   196    | app (f a : Term)
   197    /-- `fun (_ : ty) => body` -/
   198    | lam (ty body : Term)
   199    /-- `(_ : ty) → body` -/
   200    | pi (ty body : Term)
   201    /-- `let _ := val; body`, **without the type**: the body is under one
   202    binder, read at the value -/
   203    | letE (val body : Term)
   204    /-- `@Eq _ lhs rhs`, **without the type**: the interpretation is
   205    `⟦eqE a b⟧ = eqv ⟦a⟧ ⟦b⟧`, so soundness never constrains the type,
   206    and no definition and no theorem in any tier reads the type, so
   207    the constructor does not carry it; a producer that knows the type
   208    simply drops it. -/
   209    | eqE (lhs rhs : Term)
   210    /-- First field of a pair.  Carries **only** the subject: the pair's
   211    type arguments come from the typing premise `Γ ⊢ p : Σ A B`,
   212    not from the term — see the module docstring.  Interpreted by
   213    `sfst`, i.e. literally `interp`'s clause. -/
   214    | fst (e : Term)
   215    /-- Second field of a pair; the `fst` twin, interpreted by `ssnd`. -/
   216    | snd (e : Term)
   217    /-- the canonical (irrelevant) proof of a derivable equation -/
   218    | prf
   219    deriving Repr, Inhabited

== ConLeche/Semantics/Interp.lean#L134-L145
   134  noncomputable def interp : (Nat → V) → Term → V
   135    | ρ, .bvar i => ρ i
   136    | _, .sort u => univ u
   137    | _, .const c us => bval V c us
   138    | ρ, .app f a => SetTheory.app (interp ρ f) (interp ρ a)
   139    | ρ, .lam A b => lamV (interp ρ A) fun x => interp (cons x ρ) b
   140    | ρ, .pi A B => piV (interp ρ A) fun x => interp (cons x ρ) B
   141    | ρ, .letE v b => interp (cons (interp ρ v) ρ) b
   142    | ρ, .eqE a b => eqv (interp ρ a) (interp ρ b)
   143    | ρ, .fst e => sfst (interp ρ e)
   144    | ρ, .snd e => ssnd (interp ρ e)
   145    | _, .prf => pt

== ConLeche/Semantics/WellDenoted.lean#L49-L72
    49  def WellDenoted : (Nat → V) → Term → Prop
    50    | ρ, .pi A B =>
    51      WellDenoted ρ A ∧ IsTy (interp V ρ A) ∧
    52      (∀ x, x ∈ˢ interp V ρ A → WellDenoted (cons x ρ) B) ∧
    53      (∀ x, x ∈ˢ interp V ρ A → IsTy (interp V (cons x ρ) B))
    54    | ρ, .lam A b =>
    55      WellDenoted ρ A ∧ IsTy (interp V ρ A) ∧
    56      (∀ x, x ∈ˢ interp V ρ A → WellDenoted (cons x ρ) b)
    57    | ρ, .app f a =>
    58      WellDenoted ρ f ∧ WellDenoted ρ a ∧ AppliesTo (interp V ρ f) (interp V ρ a)
    59    | ρ, .fst e =>
    60      WellDenoted ρ e ∧
    61      ∃ u v A Bf, interp V ρ e ∈ˢ sigmaSet (Nat.max u v) A Bf ∧
    62        A ∈ˢ univ u ∧ ∀ x, x ∈ˢ A → Bf x ∈ˢ univ v
    63    | ρ, .snd e =>
    64      WellDenoted ρ e ∧
    65      ∃ u v A Bf, interp V ρ e ∈ˢ sigmaSet (Nat.max u v) A Bf ∧
    66        A ∈ˢ univ u ∧ ∀ x, x ∈ˢ A → Bf x ∈ˢ univ v
    67    | ρ, .eqE a b => WellDenoted ρ a ∧ WellDenoted ρ b
    68    | ρ, .letE v b => WellDenoted ρ v ∧ WellDenoted (cons (interp V ρ v) ρ) b
    69    | _, .bvar _ => True
    70    | _, .sort _ => True
    71    | _, .const _ _ => True
    72    | _, .prf => True

== ConLeche/Semantics/WellDenoted.lean#L123-L287
   123  /-! ### The substitution metatheory -/
   124  
   125  /-- Truthfulness through lifting. -/
   126  theorem WellDenoted_liftN (n : Nat) :
   127      ∀ (e : Term) (k : Nat) (ρ : Nat → V),
   128        WellDenoted V ρ (e.liftN n k) ↔ WellDenoted V (shiftE n k ρ) e := by
   129    intro e
   130    induction e with
   131    | bvar i =>
   132      intro k ρ
   133      simp only [Term.liftN_bvar]
   134      split <;> simp
   135    | sort u => intro k ρ; simp
   136    | const c us => intro k ρ; simp
   137    | app f a ihf iha =>
   138      intro k ρ
   139      rw [Term.liftN_app, WellDenoted_app, WellDenoted_app, ihf, iha,
   140        interp_liftN, interp_liftN]
   141    | lam A b ihA ihb =>
   142      intro k ρ
   143      rw [Term.liftN_lam, WellDenoted_lam, WellDenoted_lam, ihA, interp_liftN]
   144      refine and_congr Iff.rfl (and_congr Iff.rfl
   145        (forall_congr' fun x => imp_congr Iff.rfl ?_))
   146      rw [ihb, cons_shiftE]
   147    | pi A B ihA ihB =>
   148      intro k ρ
   149      rw [Term.liftN_pi, WellDenoted_pi, WellDenoted_pi, ihA, interp_liftN]
   150      refine and_congr Iff.rfl (and_congr Iff.rfl (and_congr
   151        (forall_congr' fun x => imp_congr Iff.rfl ?_)
   152        (forall_congr' fun x => imp_congr Iff.rfl ?_)))
   153      · rw [ihB, cons_shiftE]
   154      · rw [interp_liftN, cons_shiftE]
   155    | letE v b ihv ihb =>
   156      intro k ρ
   157      rw [Term.liftN_letE, WellDenoted_letE, WellDenoted_letE, ihv,
   158        interp_liftN, ihb, cons_shiftE]
   159    | eqE a b iha ihb =>
   160      intro k ρ
   161      rw [Term.liftN_eqE, WellDenoted_eqE, WellDenoted_eqE, iha, ihb]
   162    | fst e ihe =>
   163      intro k ρ
   164      rw [Term.liftN_fst, WellDenoted_fst, WellDenoted_fst, ihe,
   165        interp_liftN]
   166    | snd e ihe =>
   167      intro k ρ
   168      rw [Term.liftN_snd, WellDenoted_snd, WellDenoted_snd, ihe,
   169        interp_liftN]
   170    | prf => intro k ρ; simp
   171  
   172  /-- Truthfulness through instantiation. -/
   173  theorem WellDenoted_inst :
   174      ∀ (e a : Term) (k : Nat) (ρ : Nat → V),
   175        WellDenoted V (shiftE k 0 ρ) a →
   176        (WellDenoted V ρ (e.inst a k) ↔
   177          WellDenoted V (instE k (interp V (shiftE k 0 ρ) a) ρ) e) := by
   178    intro e
   179    induction e with
   180    | bvar i =>
   181      intro a k ρ ha
   182      show WellDenoted V ρ
   183          (if i < k then .bvar i
   184           else if i = k then Term.liftN k a else .bvar (i - 1)) ↔ _
   185      by_cases h : i < k
   186      · simp [ite_eq_left h]
   187      · by_cases h2 : i = k
   188        · simp only [ite_eq_right h, ite_eq_left h2, WellDenoted_bvar, iff_true]
   189          exact (WellDenoted_liftN V k a 0 ρ).mpr ha
   190        · simp [ite_eq_right h, ite_eq_right h2]
   191    | sort u => intro a k ρ _; simp [Term.inst]
   192    | const c us => intro a k ρ _; simp [Term.inst]
   193    | app f b ihf ihb =>
   194      intro a k ρ ha
   195      rw [Term.inst_app, WellDenoted_app, WellDenoted_app, ihf a k ρ ha,
   196        ihb a k ρ ha, interp_inst, interp_inst]
   197    | lam A b ihA ihb =>
   198      intro a k ρ ha
   199      rw [Term.inst_lam, WellDenoted_lam, WellDenoted_lam, ihA a k ρ ha,
   200        interp_inst]
   201      refine and_congr Iff.rfl (and_congr Iff.rfl
   202        (forall_congr' fun x => imp_congr Iff.rfl ?_))
   203      have ha' : WellDenoted V (shiftE (k + 1) 0 (cons x ρ)) a := by
   204        rw [shiftE_succ_cons]; exact ha
   205      rw [ihb a (k + 1) (cons x ρ) ha', shiftE_succ_cons, cons_instE]
   206    | pi A B ihA ihB =>
   207      intro a k ρ ha
   208      rw [Term.inst_pi, WellDenoted_pi, WellDenoted_pi, ihA a k ρ ha,
   209        interp_inst]
   210      refine and_congr Iff.rfl (and_congr Iff.rfl (and_congr
   211        (forall_congr' fun x => imp_congr Iff.rfl ?_)
   212        (forall_congr' fun x => imp_congr Iff.rfl ?_)))
   213      · have ha' : WellDenoted V (shiftE (k + 1) 0 (cons x ρ)) a := by
   214          rw [shiftE_succ_cons]; exact ha
   215        rw [ihB a (k + 1) (cons x ρ) ha', shiftE_succ_cons, cons_instE]
   216      · rw [interp_inst, shiftE_succ_cons, cons_instE]
   217    | letE v b ihv ihb =>
   218      intro a k ρ ha
   219      rw [Term.inst_letE, WellDenoted_letE, WellDenoted_letE, ihv a k ρ ha,
   220        interp_inst]
   221      refine and_congr Iff.rfl ?_
   222      have ha' : WellDenoted V (shiftE (k + 1) 0
   223          (cons (interp V (instE k (interp V (shiftE k 0 ρ) a) ρ) v) ρ)) a := by
   224        rw [shiftE_succ_cons]; exact ha
   225      rw [ihb a (k + 1) _ ha', shiftE_succ_cons, cons_instE]
   226    | eqE x y ihx ihy =>
   227      intro a k ρ ha
   228      rw [Term.inst_eqE, WellDenoted_eqE, WellDenoted_eqE, ihx a k ρ ha,
   229        ihy a k ρ ha]
   230    | fst e ihe =>
   231      intro a k ρ ha
   232      rw [Term.inst_fst, WellDenoted_fst, WellDenoted_fst, ihe a k ρ ha,
   233        interp_inst]
   234    | snd e ihe =>
   235      intro a k ρ ha
   236      rw [Term.inst_snd, WellDenoted_snd, WellDenoted_snd, ihe a k ρ ha,
   237        interp_inst]
   238    | prf => intro a k ρ _; simp [Term.inst]
   239  
   240  /-- Substitution at the outermost binder — the β/ζ transport form. -/
   241  theorem WellDenoted_inst0 {e a : Term} {ρ : Nat → V}
   242      (ha : WellDenoted V ρ a) :
   243      WellDenoted V ρ (e.inst a) ↔
   244        WellDenoted V (cons (interp V ρ a) ρ) e := by
   245    have h := WellDenoted_inst V e a 0 ρ (by rwa [shiftE_zero_zero])
   246    rwa [shiftE_zero_zero, instE_zero] at h
   247  
   248  /-- **ζ, graded**: a `let` interprets as its reduct, and with its value
   249  graded it is graded exactly when its reduct is.  Unconditional: no
   250  binder, so no regime. -/
   251  theorem interp_zeta (v b : Term) (ρ : Nat → V) :
   252      interp V ρ (.letE v b) = interp V ρ (b.inst v) := by
   253    rw [interp_letE, interp_inst0]
   254  
   255  theorem WellDenoted_zeta {v b : Term} {ρ : Nat → V}
   256      (hv : WellDenoted V ρ v) :
   257      WellDenoted V ρ (.letE v b) ↔ WellDenoted V ρ (b.inst v) := by
   258    rw [WellDenoted_letE, WellDenoted_inst0 V hv]
   259    exact and_iff_right hv
   260  
   261  /-! ### The graded β step
   262  
   263  At a redex that is not the point, from the subject's `WellDenoted`
   264  alone: the λ is not the point (`app_pt`), so it is a graph and the
   265  application clause reads the argument off the graph: it lies in the
   266  λ's domain (`appliesTo_graph`), and β is `app_lamV`.  At the point there
   267  is nothing to show: the claims that read this are conditional on "not
   268  the point". -/
   269  
   270  /-- **The graded β step** at a redex that is not the point. -/
   271  theorem WellDenoted_beta {A b a : Term} {ρ : Nat → V}
   272      (h : WellDenoted V ρ (.app (.lam A b) a))
   273      (hne : interp V ρ (.app (.lam A b) a) ≠ pt) :
   274      interp V ρ a ∈ˢ interp V ρ A ∧
   275      interp V ρ (.app (.lam A b) a) = interp V ρ (b.inst a) ∧
   276      WellDenoted V ρ (b.inst a) := by
   277    rw [WellDenoted_app] at h
   278    obtain ⟨hlam, ha, hap⟩ := h
   279    have hlne : interp V ρ (.lam A b) ≠ pt := by
   280      intro h0; apply hne; rw [interp_app, h0, app_pt]
   281    obtain ⟨-, -, hbody⟩ := (WellDenoted_lam V ρ A b).mp hlam
   282    have hgraph : interp V ρ (.lam A b) = graph (fun x => interp V (cons x ρ) b) (interp V ρ A) := by
   283      rw [interp_lam] at hlne ⊢; exact lamV_eq_graph hlne
   284    have haA : interp V ρ a ∈ˢ interp V ρ A := by
   285      rw [hgraph] at hap; exact (appliesTo_graph.mp hap).2
   286    refine ⟨haA, ?_, (WellDenoted_inst0 V ha).mpr (hbody _ haA)⟩
   287    rw [interp_app, interp_lam, app_lamV haA, interp_inst0]

== ConLeche/Model/Env/EnvModel.lean#L35-L63
    35  structure EnvModel (env : Env) where
    36    /-- the shared, model-free environment well-formedness -/
    37    wf : EnvWF env
    38    /-- the leaf valuation: each constant's reading at a level assignment -/
    39    acval : Name → (Name → Nat) → Term
    40    /-- every leaf is closed -/
    41    cval_closed : ∀ (n : Name) (ψ : Name → Nat),
    42      Term.Closed (acval n ψ)
    43    /-- the reserved basis constants are the pinned declarations, valued
    44    by their direct pins (V-free) -/
    45    basis_pinned : BasisPinnedTT env acval
    46    /-- every stored native projection-table entry is a pinned pair
    47    entry with its block stored (V-free, shared) -/
    48    proj_ok : ProjOkT env
    49    /-- every stored recursor rule's constructor is stored (V-free,
    50    shared) -/
    51    rec_ctors : RecCtorsStored env
    52    /-- a leaf reads only its own level parameters -/
    53    acval_params : ∀ (n : Name) (ci : ConstantInfo),
    54      env.find? n = some ci →
    55      ∀ ψ₁ ψ₂ : Name → Nat,
    56        (∀ p ∈ ci.toConstantVal.levelParams, ψ₁ p = ψ₂ p) →
    57        acval n ψ₁ = acval n ψ₂
    58    /-- every leaf is truthful -/
    59    acval_wellDenoted : ∀ (n : Name) (ψ : Name → Nat) (ρ : Nat → V),
    60      WellDenoted V ρ (acval n ψ)

== ConLeche/Model/Claims.lean#L49-L125
    49  /-- Head normalisation, dual success, P currency, conditional on the
    50  point (task #342, L9): the reduct is graded and equal where the subject
    51  is not the point. -/
    52  @[expose] def WhnfCoreClaim {env : Env} (m : EnvModel V env)
    53      (φ : Name → Nat) (fuel : Nat) : Prop :=
    54    ∀ {d : Nat} {e e' : Expr} {Δa : List Term},
    55      whnfCore .verified false env fuel d e = .ok e' →
    56      Expr.WScoped d e → e.looseBVarsBounded 0 = true →
    57      Expr.LeavesBounded e →
    58      ∀ {ea ea' : Term},
    59        CtxOk m φ d Δa e →
    60        denote m.acval env φ d e = some ea →
    61        denote m.acval env φ d e' = some ea' →
    62        (∀ ρ : Nat → V, Sat V Δa ρ → WellDenoted V ρ ea) →
    63        (∀ ρ : Nat → V, Sat V Δa ρ → interp V ρ ea ≠ pt →
    64            WellDenoted V ρ ea') ∧
    65          ∀ ρ : Nat → V, Sat V Δa ρ → interp V ρ ea ≠ pt →
    66            interp V ρ ea = interp V ρ ea'
    67  
    68  /-- The reduction loop, dual success, P currency, conditional on the
    69  point (task #342, L9). -/
    70  @[expose] def WhnfClaim {env : Env} (m : EnvModel V env)
    71      (φ : Name → Nat) (fuel : Nat) : Prop :=
    72    ∀ {d : Nat} {e e' : Expr} {Δa : List Term},
    73      whnf .verified false env fuel d e = .ok e' →
    74      Expr.WScoped d e → e.looseBVarsBounded 0 = true →
    75      Expr.LeavesBounded e →
    76      ∀ {ea ea' : Term},
    77        CtxOk m φ d Δa e →
    78        denote m.acval env φ d e = some ea →
    79        denote m.acval env φ d e' = some ea' →
    80        (∀ ρ : Nat → V, Sat V Δa ρ → WellDenoted V ρ ea) →
    81        (∀ ρ : Nat → V, Sat V Δa ρ → interp V ρ ea ≠ pt →
    82            WellDenoted V ρ ea') ∧
    83          ∀ ρ : Nat → V, Sat V Δa ρ → interp V ρ ea ≠ pt →
    84            interp V ρ ea = interp V ρ ea'
    85  
    86  /-- Definitional equality, P currency, conditional on the point (task
    87  #342, L9): two sides that are not the point are equal.  A consumer
    88  comparing two types or two members of one type closes with
    89  `eq_of_IsTy_of_ne_pt` / `IsTy.eq_of_ne_pt`. -/
    90  @[expose] def DefEqClaim {env : Env} (m : EnvModel V env)
    91      (φ : Name → Nat) (fuel : Nat) : Prop :=
    92    ∀ {d : Nat} {a b : Expr} {Δa : List Term},
    93      ConLeche.isDefEqCore .verified false env fuel d a b = .ok true →
    94      Expr.WScoped d a → a.looseBVarsBounded 0 = true →
    95      Expr.LeavesBounded a →
    96      Expr.WScoped d b → b.looseBVarsBounded 0 = true →
    97      Expr.LeavesBounded b →
    98      ∀ {aa ba : Term},
    99        CtxOk m φ d Δa a →
   100        CtxOk m φ d Δa b →
   101        denote m.acval env φ d a = some aa →
   102        denote m.acval env φ d b = some ba →
   103        (∀ ρ : Nat → V, Sat V Δa ρ → WellDenoted V ρ aa) →
   104        (∀ ρ : Nat → V, Sat V Δa ρ → WellDenoted V ρ ba) →
   105        ∀ ρ : Nat → V, Sat V Δa ρ →
   106          interp V ρ aa ≠ pt → interp V ρ ba ≠ pt →
   107          interp V ρ aa = interp V ρ ba
   108  
   109  /-- Inference, dual success, P currency: the subject's and the
   110  type's truthfulness are *conclusions*, and
   111  the type denotes a type. -/
   112  @[expose] def InferClaim {env : Env} (m : EnvModel V env)
   113      (φ : Name → Nat) (fuel : Nat) : Prop :=
   114    ∀ {d : Nat} {e t : Expr} {Δa : List Term},
   115      inferTypeCore .verified false env fuel d e = .ok t →
   116      Expr.WScoped d e → e.looseBVarsBounded 0 = true →
   117      Expr.LeavesBounded e →
   118      ∀ {ea ta : Term},
   119        CtxOk m φ d Δa e →
   120        denote m.acval env φ d e = some ea →
   121        denote m.acval env φ d t = some ta →
   122        (∀ ρ : Nat → V, Sat V Δa ρ → WellDenoted V ρ ea) ∧
   123          (∀ ρ : Nat → V, Sat V Δa ρ → WellDenotedTy V ρ ta) ∧
   124          ∀ ρ : Nat → V, Sat V Δa ρ →
   125            interp V ρ ea ∈ˢ interp V ρ ta

== ConLeche/Rules/Rel.lean#L107-L111
   107  
   108  /-- **Reduction**: the head steps of `whnfCore` and the `whnf` loop,
   109  chained. -/
   110  inductive Red (env : Env) : Nat → Expr → Expr → Prop where
   111    /-- Every `pure e` exit: the value clauses of `whnfCoreBody`

== ConLeche/Rules/Rel.lean#L365-L388
   365  checker only ever compares terms that are well-formed *together* — a
   366  fact the rules never state, because well-formedness (scoping, the
   367  readability of the terms, the grading of the reading) is semantic
   368  and may not enter this inductive.  Every rule respects one syntactic
   369  discipline instead: **the subject of each `DefEq` premise is either a
   370  subterm of the conclusion or is produced by an existence-form `Red` /
   371  `Infer` premise** (a reduct, an inferred type), so the soundness proof
   372  (`ConLeche/Model/Rules/Sound.lean`) always has the premise's terms in
   373  hand.  `trans` is the unique rule that would break it: its middle
   374  term comes from nowhere, and with it two rules that are each sound
   375  alone meet — `fvar` compares free variables by index only (their
   376  types are not compared, as the checker does not), while
   377  `proofFast` *reads* a head's stored data to decide "definitely a
   378  proof" — and derive `DefEq env d (.fvar i ty) (.fvar i' ty')` for
   379  every `i`, `i'`, which no model satisfies.  The recursive-structure rules
   380  (`redL`, `natSucc`, `eta`, `structUnit`) are therefore not a
   381  proof-engineering convenience but what keeps the relation sound; the
   382  one chaining that is sound, "reduce, then continue", is `redL`, and
   383  its right-hand and δ variants are derived in `Derived.lean`. -/
   384  inductive DefEq (env : Env) : Nat → Expr → Expr → Prop where
   385    /-- The syntactic fast paths (`defeqBody`, `quickDefEq`),
   386    the literal leaf (`:1582`), a same-index `fvar` pair is `fvar`
   387    below. -/
   388    | refl {d : Nat} {a : Expr} : DefEq env d a a

== ConLeche/Kernel/CoreDefs.lean#L544-L552
   544  /-- The certified structural-`Nat` operations.  Six of them
   545  (`add sub mul pow beq ble`) carry a literal fast path; `Nat.pred` is
   546  here without one — it has no fast path (official's `reduce_nat` folds
   547  nothing unary but `Nat.succ`), but `Nat.sub`'s recurrence
   548  `sub x (succ y) = pred (sub x y)` names it, so its own recurrences
   549  must be certified for `sub`'s literal fold to be sound. -/

   480    else if c.name = listConsName then listConsTyOk (some c)

   485  /-! ## Structural-Nat literal acceleration
   486  
   487  The official kernel accelerates the structural `Nat` operations on
   488  literals (GMP-backed there).  Here the fast path is *certified*: an
   489  operation participates only when its defining recurrence equations
   490  hold by definitional equality — checked once, at its check: `checkDecl`
   491  positively rejects a nonstandard definition under one of these names,
   492  so *presence in the store is the certificate* (no runtime flag, no
   493  re-checking; a reduction-time re-check would in fact livelock — the
   494  certification's own `pred zero` equation re-enters the fast path).

   496  The certification runs in the environment *before* the operation is

   106      List (Expr × Expr) → m Bool
   107    | [] => pure true
   108    | eq :: rest => do
   109      if ← ops.isDefEq env 2 eq.1 eq.2 then

   111      else pure false

== ConLeche/Cached/StateC.lean#L252-L265
   252  compute.  `a ^ b` has at most `natSizeBytes a * b` bytes, and a base
   253  `≤ 1` gives `0` or `1`; `a <<< b` has about `natSizeBytes a + b / 8`
   254  bytes, and `0 <<< b = 0`. -/
   255  def natOpRefusal (maxNatSize : Nat) (op : NatBinOp) (a b : Nat) : Option CheckError :=
   256    match op with
   257    | .pow =>
   258      if b > natCountMax then some (natCountTooBig "Nat.pow")
   259      else if a > 1 && b != 0 && natSizeBytes a > maxNatSize / b then
   260        some (.invalid "the kernel refused to evaluate `Nat.pow` because the result would \
   261          exceed the maximum numeral size; raise it with --max-nat-size")
   262      else none
   263    | .shiftLeft =>
   264      if a = 0 then none
   265      else if b > natCountMax then some (natCountTooBig "Nat.shiftLeft")

== ConLeche/Kernel/CoreDefs.lean#L675-L695
   675  def natOpResult (c : Name) (a b : Nat) : Option Expr :=
   676    if c = natPredName then some (.lit (.natVal (a - 1)))
   677    else if c = natAddName then some (.lit (.natVal (a + b)))
   678    else if c = natSubName then some (.lit (.natVal (a - b)))
   679    else if c = natMulName then some (.lit (.natVal (a * b)))
   680    else if c = natPowName then some (.lit (.natVal (a ^ b)))
   681    else if c = natDivName then some (.lit (.natVal (a / b)))
   682    else if c = natModName then some (.lit (.natVal (a % b)))
   683    else if c = natGcdName then some (.lit (.natVal (Nat.gcd a b)))
   684    else if c = natLandName then some (.lit (.natVal (Nat.land a b)))
   685    else if c = natLorName then some (.lit (.natVal (Nat.lor a b)))
   686    else if c = natXorName then some (.lit (.natVal (Nat.xor a b)))
   687    else if c = natShiftLeftName then
   688      some (.lit (.natVal (Nat.shiftLeft a b)))
   689    else if c = natShiftRightName then
   690      some (.lit (.natVal (Nat.shiftRight a b)))
   691    else if c = natBeqName then
   692      some (.const (if a = b then boolTrueName else boolFalseName) [])
   693    else if c = natBleName then
   694      some (.const (if a <= b then boolTrueName else boolFalseName) [])
   695    else none

== ConLeche/SetTheory/Core.lean#L95-L156
    95  /-- A model of set theory of exactly the strength the checker needs:
    96  membership, the six ZF⁻ axioms (extensionality, pairing, union, power
    97  set, regularity, Lean-level replacement), and an ω-chain of
    98  Grothendieck universes.  Infinity is derivable; choice is inherited
    99  from the meta-logic (`Classical.choice`); see the module docstring. -/
   100  class SetTheory (V : Type u) where
   101    /-- Set membership. -/
   102    Mem : V → V → Prop
   103    /-- Extensionality: sets with the same members are equal. -/
   104    ext : ∀ {x y : V}, (∀ z, Mem z x ↔ Mem z y) → x = y
   105    /-- Pairing: the unordered pair. -/
   106    upair : V → V → V
   107    /-- Characterization of the unordered pair. -/
   108    mem_upair : ∀ {z a b : V}, Mem z (upair a b) ↔ z = a ∨ z = b
   109    /-- Union: the union of the members. -/
   110    sUnion : V → V
   111    /-- Characterization of the union. -/
   112    mem_sUnion : ∀ {z x : V}, Mem z (sUnion x) ↔ ∃ y, Mem y x ∧ Mem z y
   113    /-- Power set. -/
   114    power : V → V
   115    /-- Characterization of the power set: members are the subsets. -/
   116    mem_power : ∀ {z x : V}, Mem z (power x) ↔ ∀ w, Mem w z → Mem w x
   117    /-- Regularity: every nonempty set has an `∈`-minimal member. -/
   118    regularity : ∀ x : V, (∃ y, Mem y x) → ∃ y, Mem y x ∧ ¬ ∃ z, Mem z y ∧ Mem z x
   119    /-- Replacement, as a Lean-level scheme: the image of a set under an
   120    arbitrary function `V → V`. -/
   121    image : (V → V) → V → V
   122    /-- Characterization of the replacement image. -/
   123    mem_image : ∀ {f : V → V} {a z : V}, Mem z (image f a) ↔ ∃ w, Mem w a ∧ z = f w
   124    /-- An ω-chain of Grothendieck universes: the sets interpreting the
   125    universe tower (Carneiro's ω-many inaccessibles, op. cit.;
   126    intended model `V_{κ n}`). -/
   127    univChain : Nat → V
   128    /-- The chain increases strictly: each universe is a member of the
   129    next. -/
   130    univChain_mem : ∀ n : Nat, Mem (univChain n) (univChain (n + 1))
   131    /-- Each chain member is a Grothendieck universe (Tarski's Axiom A
   132    matrix with transitivity, `IsTGUniverse`). -/
   133    univChain_tg : ∀ n : Nat, IsTGUniverse Mem (univChain n)
   134  
   135  namespace SetTheory
   136  
   137  @[inherit_doc] scoped infix:50 " ∈ˢ " => Mem
   138  
   139  variable {V : Type u} [SetTheory V]
   140  
   141  /-- Subset, from membership. -/
   142  protected def Subset (x y : V) : Prop := ∀ z, z ∈ˢ x → z ∈ˢ y
   143  
   144  @[inherit_doc] scoped infix:50 " ⊆ˢ " => SetTheory.Subset
   145  
   146  theorem Subset.refl (x : V) : x ⊆ˢ x := fun _ hz => hz
   147  
   148  theorem Subset.trans {x y z : V} (h₁ : x ⊆ˢ y) (h₂ : y ⊆ˢ z) : x ⊆ˢ z :=
   149    fun w hw => h₂ w (h₁ w hw)
   150  
   151  theorem Subset.antisymm {x y : V} (h₁ : x ⊆ˢ y) (h₂ : y ⊆ˢ x) : x = y :=
   152    ext fun z => ⟨h₁ z, h₂ z⟩
   153  
   154  theorem mem_power_iff_subset {z x : V} : z ∈ˢ power x ↔ z ⊆ˢ x := mem_power
   155  
   156  end SetTheory

== ConLeche/Kernel/TrustAxioms.lean#L9-L38
     9  /-!
    10  # The compiler-trust axiom family (task #95)
    11  
    12  `Init`'s compiler-trust scaffolding is installed rather than
    13  declined:
    14  
    15  * `Lean.trustCompiler : True` is trivially realizable — it is
    16    installed as an *opaque* (stored `axiomInfo`, exactly like a checked
    17    `opaque` declaration) with value `True.intro`, over a pinned `True`
    18    family.  No new meta-axiom: the model is `True.intro`'s own
    19    interpretation.
    20  * `Lean.reduceNat` / `Lean.reduceBool` then check as ordinary
    21    `opaque`s (their exported values are identity functions modulo the
    22    `have := trustCompiler` wrapper); at its check their stored values are
    23    pinned against the identity function
    24    (`ConLeche/Kernel/TrustPins.lean`, hand-pinned since task #273 —
    25    every toolchain's definition after zeta) by definitional equality —
    26    the task-#47 pattern: drift declines, never silently.
    27  * `Lean.ofReduceNat` / `Lean.ofReduceBool` are pinned axioms over
    28    those stored opaques (the task-#34 standard-axioms machinery).  With
    29    the stored reduce operation certified to be the identity (a
    30    definitional-equality certificate at the operation's own install,
    31    `checkReducePin`; the axiom's install checks `ofReduceAxOk`),
    32    `∀ a b, reduceNat a = b → a = b` interprets to
    33    an inhabited proposition (the hypothesis *is* the conclusion), so
    34    both axioms are true in the set model with the proof point as value.
    35  
    36  `sorryAx` remains the only axiom tolerated as a *declaration*: its
    37  record installs nothing and any use of it declines
    38  (`sorryAxName`, `ConLeche/Kernel/Basis/Names.lean`).

== ConLeche/Denotes.lean#L248-L268
   248  structure Model (V : Type w) [SetTheory V] (env : Env) where
   249    /-- the set a constant denotes, per level assignment -/
   250    cval : Name → (LevelParam → Nat) → V
   251    /-- every stored constant is a member of what its type denotes, at
   252    every level assignment (and every variable environment — the type
   253    is closed) -/
   254    mem : ∀ c ∈ env.consts, ∀ (φ : LevelParam → Nat) (ρ : BVarIdx → V),
   255      ∃ T, Denotes cval env φ ρ c.toConstantVal.type T ∧ cval c.name φ ∈ˢ T
   256    /-- whatever the built-in `False` denotes is the empty set -/
   257    false_empty : ∀ (φ : LevelParam → Nat) (ρ : BVarIdx → V) (F : V),
   258      Denotes cval env φ ρ (.const falseName []) F → F = empty
   259    /-- whatever the built-in `Eq` denotes is set equality: at a type `A`
   260    of the universe the level `u` names, and two of its members `a` and
   261    `b`, `@Eq.{u} A a b` denotes the truth value of `a = b`.  The three
   262    membership premises are the graph's domains — `Eq`'s denotation is a
   263    three-fold graph over `univ (Level.eval φ u)`, then over `A`, then
   264    over `A` again, and a graph read off its domain says nothing -/
   265    eq_equality : ∀ (u : Level) (φ : LevelParam → Nat) (ρ : BVarIdx → V) (E A a b : V),
   266      Denotes cval env φ ρ (.const eqName [u]) E →
   267      A ∈ˢ univ (Level.eval φ u) → a ∈ˢ A → b ∈ˢ A →
   268      app (app (app E A) a) b = eqv a b

== ConLeche/SetTheory/Core.lean#L95-L133
    95  /-- A model of set theory of exactly the strength the checker needs:
    96  membership, the six ZF⁻ axioms (extensionality, pairing, union, power
    97  set, regularity, Lean-level replacement), and an ω-chain of
    98  Grothendieck universes.  Infinity is derivable; choice is inherited
    99  from the meta-logic (`Classical.choice`); see the module docstring. -/
   100  class SetTheory (V : Type u) where
   101    /-- Set membership. -/
   102    Mem : V → V → Prop
   103    /-- Extensionality: sets with the same members are equal. -/
   104    ext : ∀ {x y : V}, (∀ z, Mem z x ↔ Mem z y) → x = y
   105    /-- Pairing: the unordered pair. -/
   106    upair : V → V → V
   107    /-- Characterization of the unordered pair. -/
   108    mem_upair : ∀ {z a b : V}, Mem z (upair a b) ↔ z = a ∨ z = b
   109    /-- Union: the union of the members. -/
   110    sUnion : V → V
   111    /-- Characterization of the union. -/
   112    mem_sUnion : ∀ {z x : V}, Mem z (sUnion x) ↔ ∃ y, Mem y x ∧ Mem z y
   113    /-- Power set. -/
   114    power : V → V
   115    /-- Characterization of the power set: members are the subsets. -/
   116    mem_power : ∀ {z x : V}, Mem z (power x) ↔ ∀ w, Mem w z → Mem w x
   117    /-- Regularity: every nonempty set has an `∈`-minimal member. -/
   118    regularity : ∀ x : V, (∃ y, Mem y x) → ∃ y, Mem y x ∧ ¬ ∃ z, Mem z y ∧ Mem z x
   119    /-- Replacement, as a Lean-level scheme: the image of a set under an
   120    arbitrary function `V → V`. -/
   121    image : (V → V) → V → V
   122    /-- Characterization of the replacement image. -/
   123    mem_image : ∀ {f : V → V} {a z : V}, Mem z (image f a) ↔ ∃ w, Mem w a ∧ z = f w
   124    /-- An ω-chain of Grothendieck universes: the sets interpreting the
   125    universe tower (Carneiro's ω-many inaccessibles, op. cit.;
   126    intended model `V_{κ n}`). -/
   127    univChain : Nat → V
   128    /-- The chain increases strictly: each universe is a member of the
   129    next. -/
   130    univChain_mem : ∀ n : Nat, Mem (univChain n) (univChain (n + 1))
   131    /-- Each chain member is a Grothendieck universe (Tarski's Axiom A
   132    matrix with transitivity, `IsTGUniverse`). -/
   133    univChain_tg : ∀ n : Nat, IsTGUniverse Mem (univChain n)
